pr.title: Review Projector's own pull requests in GitHub Actions
pr.head: 2fe07a7e5a45f8e033e8a347b8cd4f0a271c70a7

summary: Projector currently reviews this repository’s pull requests from agent sessions. This layer enables the same review flow on GitHub-hosted runners, so ready pull requests with a branch in this repository can receive a review without a laptop session.

The workflow checks this repository out and runs Claude through the review action in that checkout, so pull requests that change the action can exercise it before merge. A separate job publishes the resulting review page. The settings identify the workflow’s bot as a trusted source of Projector verdicts, and a runner-specific gate override retains the exact-head CI check.

cards.title: Complete the credential-backed rollout
cards.html:
• The local action starts from this pull request’s checkout, so it does not need the action on main first.
  • A credential secret is now set: the hosted review job runs the agent and posts its verdict as github-actions[bot].
  • The hosted-runner facts that § 7 of the plan lists still need recording from these first runs.

cards.title: Review evidence
cards.html:
• The hosted review of 2fe07a7 ran the workflow’s gate override: both plugin validations and the whitespace check passed, and the exact-head check workflow passed.
  • That review also ran claude plugin test . on the runner: all 256 hook tests passed without the interactive session’s declarations.
  • It requested changes on one finding: the override’s gate leaves out the hook tests, which no other CI job runs. See the flag under the workflow’s gate line.

groups.title: Count the workflow’s reviews
groups.kicker: Enable CI review and recognize its bot
intro: A review posted by github-actions[bot] is not a human collaborator’s review. Public repositories ignore verdicts from untrusted accounts, so enabling the workflow also records that this bot’s Projector verdicts count.

The settings select Claude and enable later init refreshes. Once they reach the default branch, sessions, the panel, and the site can use the bot’s verdict in the same sign-off calculation as other trusted reviews.

files.note: Enable CI reviews with Claude and add the Actions bot to the counted reviewer list.

checks.text: Focused status, watch, and site tests confirm that the named bot’s verdict counts on a public repository while an unlisted account’s verdict does not.

groups.title: Review with the action in the checkout
groups.kicker: Exercise action changes before merge with separate publication permissions
intro: The review job runs for ready pull requests whose heads are in this repository and can also be started manually. Each job checks the repository out before using ./actions/review, which loads the action from the workspace. A pull-request run therefore exercises the action in its checked-out result. Each new head cancels the older review for the same pull request and agent.

Each matrix entry names an agent and can name its model. This repository’s single Claude entry leaves the model empty, so the action supplies claude-opus-5-5. The updated workflow forwards the model field through to the action instead of leaving per-agent model choices behind.

The agent’s job can post reviews and statuses but cannot push code. A second job, which runs no agent, holds the write permission needed to publish summaries. The runner also refuses drafts and fork heads, so a manual trigger does not bypass that boundary.

A review’s gate is the shell command .projector.toml names in review.gate, run on the head before a review signs it off. Projector’s local gate runs the plugin validations, the hook tests, a type-check that needs declarations only an interactive Claude Code session writes, and a whitespace check. The workflow’s config input writes an [override.50.review] table to the runner’s ~/.projector.toml, which replaces that gate with one that runs the plugin validations and the whitespace check. The existing check workflow still supplies the Python suite, the site’s lint, and the plan check.

files.note: Check out before loading the local review action in both jobs, forward per-agent models, and preserve the runner gate override.

checks.text: Traced the job condition and the runner’s own refusal: drafts and fork heads are excluded, including manual dispatch.

Both jobs check out before resolving the local action. Traced its inner checkout and setup order, then ran the real setup script with fake Git from this layout; its project shim worked without changing a remote or global Git settings.

Executed this committed workflow’s resolved Claude inputs through the action’s review script against a command stub. It reached the command with model claude-opus-5-5, without starting an agent or using credentials.

The workflow differs from the generator’s output only by the local checkout and action steps in both jobs and the five-line gate override. On the runner, project config get review.gate returns the override, review.gate_checks still waits for check, and the edited file keeps init from replacing it.

The override’s gate leaves out claude plugin test . as well as hooks/typecheck.sh, but only the type-check needs the interactive session’s declarations. The hook tests run and pass on the hosted runner, and no other CI job runs them, so a bot verdict could sign off a head whose hook tests fail. Add claude plugin test . to the override.
Exactly one of the two Claude secrets must be set. The action rejects both and neither; credential values were not read or changed during this review.
Traced the action’s two modes and the declared permissions: the review job lacks contents write, while only the summary job can push the page’s hidden ref.

groups.title: Record the action-source decision
groups.kicker: Keep the repository’s own rollout choice with the plan
intro: The plan records why Projector loads its own review action from the pull request’s checkout: the action can review the changes that build it before those changes reach the default branch. Workflows installed by init in other repositories continue to call a release reference.

files.note: Record the local-action choice for Projector’s own workflow.

checks.text: The added implementation decision matches both local-action calls in this workflow; the shared generator still writes a release-based action reference.
